policy: Main building ranges, not occupied land parcels. Use is unassigned unless explicitly labelled on the map. Two-storey elevations and divisions are estimates; no invented shop signs or tenants. Existing factory and housing footprints take precedence at registration overlaps.

vista.photo: reference/Images and Figures/PossibleCover_Three Mills Wall London Fireworks Co 1900.jpg
vista.photoDate: circa 1900, supplied filename; original archive date not independently verified
vista.orientation: Working south-facing view from the High Street end, east bank on the left; exact camera remains provisional
observed: Narrow unsurfaced path above the water on the left
Close boarded boundary fence and lower riverside timber rail
Grassy bank face with a timber-retained toe
Two-storey brick premises on the left and waterside masonry on the right
Tall gabled warehouse in the distance
vista.interpretation: The existing Sugar House is a candidate for the distant warehouse. Its identification and the exact camera need further photographic fitting. The photo establishes types and relative arrangement, not surveyed metric dimensions.
vista.limits: Path dimensions, heights, individual tree positions, timber details and all absolute offsets are photo-informed estimates attached to the existing GIS bank. No 1930s concrete embankment geometry is introduced. No photographic texture is used.

connections.evidence: Interpreted bank access to Abbey Lane/High Street, reconciled with GIS bank and provisional frontage placement; not a surveyed route.
OS five-foot map shows continuous east-bank route. Intermediate alignment follows GIS shore; junction and levels interpreted.
OS east-bank lane continues to the distillery approach; connection geometry and level inferred.
